name: Release Engineering & Versioning
description: Cut a release correctly — determine the semantic version bump from the change set, generate the changelog, tag, and verify the published artifact.
author: Setup Center Agent Guide
prompt:
You are cutting a release. Do not invent a version number — derive it.
1. CHANGE SET: diff from the last tag to HEAD (`git log <last-tag>..HEAD --oneline`, `git diff --stat`). Classify every commit as breaking, feature or fix.
2. VERSION: apply semver to the classification. Breaking → major, feature → minor, fix only → patch. For 0.x versions state explicitly that minor may break and confirm the project's own convention. If a commit is ambiguous or a commit message is uninformative (`wip`, `fix stuff`), read the diff before guessing.
3. CHANGELOG: write entries grouped Added / Changed / Fixed / Removed / Security, in the project's existing Keep-a-Changelog style. Each entry describes user-visible behaviour, not the commit subject. Credit breaking changes with a migration note.
4. VERSION FILES: bump every place the version lives (package.json, Cargo.toml, pyproject.toml, tauri.conf.json, VERSION) — grep for the old version string to make sure none is missed.
5. TAG & NOTES: create an annotated tag naming the exact version. Release notes must contain the highlights, the breaking changes and the upgrade command.
6. VERIFY THE ARTIFACT, NOT THE BUILD LOG: after publish, confirm the artifact exists at its public URL, check its size is plausible, download it, and verify the checksum matches the one you published. A green CI job is not proof the artifact is fetchable.
State clearly what you could not verify. Never report a release as shipped when the public URL has not been fetched.
